subject.title: fix(streaming): preserve paragraph separators across block-streamed deliveries [AI-assisted]

question: Should maintainers require explicit boundary metadata or another in-budget seam signal before merging, or intentionally accept this PR as a partial common-case repair?
rationale: The author and source review both show the remaining maxChars case cannot be solved by simply attaching text without either exceeding delivery limits or changing seam semantics, so a maintainer needs to choose the permanent delivery contract and which sibling PR, if any, should carry it.

options.title: Require boundary semantics before merge
options.body: Consolidate the sibling work and require an in-budget seam signal or equivalent design so paragraph reconstruction works even at maxChars boundaries.

options.title: Accept partial repair knowingly
options.body: Land the common-case text-only improvement while documenting the maxChars boundary as remaining work on the canonical issue.

options.title: Pause both candidates
options.body: Keep both open but stop merge progress until a maintainer names the preferred implementation owner and proof path.

recommendation.title: Require boundary semantics before merge
recommendation.body: Consolidate the sibling work and require an in-budget seam signal or equivalent design so paragraph reconstruction works even at maxChars boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: History ties this owner to block-reply coalescing and chunking hardening, which are the central surfaces for the boundary-semantics choice.
